findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, all in plain words. On this alone they could say what Athena is and why it matters.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: There is a link to next steps in the header, and the Next steps section is concrete: prerequisites, the clone command, `./setup.sh`, and a first command to try (`athena ask "add a changelog"`). A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: This is Athena's home page, but the title and nearly all of the body are a study of a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who clicks "Start here" expecting to learn about Athena gets firstmate's internals instead, so the page's main content serves a different reader.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title>; heading "Start here"

findings.text: The study is meant to prove Athena can explain a project with traced claims, but the page never shows Athena doing its actual job: a request, how it was read, the two models, the cost and the verdict. The lede promises all of that, and the newcomer has to take it on trust or install Athena to see it.
findings.source: This page is that study of firstmate. Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it

findings.text: These sections are dense and full of firstmate terms (exit 75, close-pending, pending-close record, captain call, mode=retain). They reward someone who already knows firstmate. A newcomer to Athena is likely to give up here, and nothing tells them they can skip ahead to Next steps.
findings.source: Headings "States of a piece of work", "Counters", "Transitions" (cards t1–t12)

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the term has no definition in the source. That is honest, but for a newcomer it reads as gaps. They still don't know what those words mean.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." / "does not define a durable record" / "does not define an endpoint" / "does not define a heartbeat" / "does not define a wake"

findings.text: The header links to an owner-only page about proposals waiting for a decision. A newcomer is not the owner, so the link is confusing and takes attention away from the next-step link above it.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: This closing note is about Athena's internal repository layout. A first-time visitor gets nothing from it.
findings.source: About this page: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."

findings.text: The Limits section openly says what the study did not run and what an early reading missed. That builds trust with a careful reader. A newcomer judging Athena may also read it as a sign that Athena's own reading is unreliable.
findings.source: f3 "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths ... none was run, so no run confirmed that a script behaves as its header says."
